inventory.name: Chrome 147 width/style decoupling (computed *-width no longer forced to 0 by *-style none|hidden)
<line-width> = <length [0,∞]> | thin | medium | thick (unchanged value grammar shared by all three properties)
border-width / border-{top,right,bottom,left}-width — computed value decoupled; resolved value explicitly the used value (0 when style none|hidden)
outline-width — computed and resolved value now reflect the authored value
column-rule-width (and list-valued column-rule-width/row-rule-width in css-gaps-1) — computed and resolved value now reflect the authored value

errors.rationale: A computed-value resolution change has no error channel: CSS declarations fail only at parse time (an invalid <line-width> drops the declaration), and the unchanged grammar is given in the syntax section. No runtime exception or rejection path exists.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The change alters how same-document style values resolve; it exposes no new cross-origin or device information. The ChromeStatus record tracks it as an interop alignment of value resolution with no security/privacy gating surface (no flag, no origin trial, enabled by default).

errors.rationale: A value type has no error surface beyond parse-time invalidity: a negative length is excluded by the [0,∞] range in the quoted grammar and simply fails to parse, dropping the declaration per standard CSS error handling.

securityPrivacy.rationale: A shared CSS value grammar (<line-width>) carries no security or privacy surface of its own; it only constrains the accepted author input for the three width properties quoted verbatim in the syntax section.

errors.rationale: border-width has no runtime error path: invalid values are dropped at parse time per the quoted grammar, and the behavior change affects only how valid declarations compute and resolve.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Border width resolution is same-document styling with no information-exposure, permission, or storage surface; the spec change (PR #11913) is purely a computed/used-value bookkeeping clarification.

errors.rationale: outline-width has no runtime error path: invalid values are dropped at parse time per the quoted grammar, and the behavior change affects only how valid declarations compute and resolve.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Outline width resolution is same-document styling with no information-exposure, permission, or storage surface; the removed computed-value special case (css-ui-4 changes list) is an interop alignment only.

errors.rationale: column-rule-width has no runtime error path: invalid values are dropped at parse time per the quoted grammar (css-gaps-1 additionally notes negative values are not allowed), and the change affects only computed/resolved values.

securityPrivacy.rationale: Column-rule width resolution is same-document styling with no information-exposure, permission, or storage surface; the css-multicol/css-gaps change moves the none|hidden zeroing from computed to used value only.

notes: Contract written during the 2026-10-04 MDN-shape upgrade. The surface is a computed/resolved-value migration on three long-shipped CSS properties; the PR #11913 diff (fetched via the repository's pull ref, commit 5e14aa0) was compared against the live editor's drafts to confirm the merge. The upgrade also corrected a factual error in the original page: getComputedStyle().borderWidth does NOT return the authored width (border-width's resolved value is explicitly the used value, 0 when style is none|hidden); only outline-width and column-rule-width resolved values change, matching the ChromeStatus summary. Firefox/Safari 'earlier' support for the border/outline part rests on the ChromeStatus summary sentence; no per-version vendor record was found for it and the compat table says so. Runtime behavior is source-derived, not executed.
